decision: The programme uses at least six inequivalent notions of gap. Only an infinite-volume continuum gauge-invariant Hamiltonian spectral gap inside a rigorously constructed compact Yang-Mills QFT addresses the Clay problem.

gapTypes.name: finiteOperator
gapTypes.object: finite Dirac, adjacency or response matrix
gapTypes.gap: minimum nonzero singular value or eigenvalue separation

gapTypes.name: vacuumHessian
gapTypes.object: quadratic fluctuation matrix at a stationary vacuum
gapTypes.gap: positive minimum physical mass-squared eigenvalue after gauge constraints
gapTypes.survivesNeeded: gauge quotient, radiative stability and continuum QFT

gapTypes.name: topologicalBand
gapTypes.gap: uniform separation between occupied and unoccupied bands
gapTypes.survivesNeeded: interactions and the proposed spacetime/internal lift

gapTypes.name: liouvillian
gapTypes.gap: smallest nonzero decay rate in minus the real spectrum
gapTypes.survivesNeeded: replacement by a closed unitary Hamiltonian theory if a particle mass is claimed

gapTypes.name: finiteLatticeTransfer
gapTypes.gap: minus log(lambda1/lambda0) divided by the Euclidean time spacing
gapTypes.survivesNeeded: uniform thermodynamic and continuum limits with reflection positivity

gapTypes.name: qftMassGap
gapTypes.object: physical Hamiltonian reconstructed from gauge-invariant Euclidean correlators
gapTypes.gap: infimum of the nonvacuum spectrum above zero

promotionGate: nontrivial interacting continuum theory on R4
Euclidean axioms including reflection positivity sufficient for reconstruction
gauge-invariant physical Hilbert space and Hamiltonian
unique vacuum or declared vacuum sector
strict positive lower bound on the complete nonvacuum spectrum

spin23Boundary.statement: Spin(2,3) is noncompact and is used as a broken spacetime Cartan group, so its whole-connection gap is neither the compact Yang-Mills problem nor compatible with an ordinary long-range massless graviton.
spin23Boundary.allowedQuestion: whether non-Einstein torsion, coset or portal sectors have positive physical gaps while the spin-2 sector remains massless
spin23Boundary.internalQuestion: the SU(3)c descendant of E6 has its own compact nonperturbative Yang-Mills/QCD gap and confinement problem
